newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SOCCER-BELGIAN POLICE DETAIN 71 AHEAD OF WORLD CUP TIE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BELGIAN POLICE DETAIN 71 AHEAD OF WORLD CUP TIE.

text.p: Belgian police said on Saturday they had detained 71 football supporters ahead of the night's World Cup clash between Belgium and the Netherlands.

"Of the 71, 58 are from the Netherlands. The rest are Belgian," police spokesman Michael Jonniaux told Reuters. "Most of them are arrests for drunkeness or showing aggressive behaviour towards shoppers and tourists."
Jonniaux said only five of the arrests were likely to result in charges being brought. "The situation is still very calm but people have only just started arriving at the stadium," he said.
Jonniaux was speaking one hour before the 2000 local (1900 GMT) kick off.
Belgian police are taking no chances with the match, deploying more than 1,500 officers, 150 mounted policemen, water cannon and 20 dog teams to patrol Brussels' metro system.
Belga news agency reported earlier that motorway police had stopped five Dutch supporters heading to Brussels carrying weapons but no identification or tickets for the match.
The match is being played at the Heysel stadium where 39 fans were crushed to death by a wall which collapsed when Juventas and Liverpool supporters clashed at a European cup final in 1985.
The stadium has since been rebuilt and renamed after former Belgian monarch King Baudouin.
